title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 55 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 410–416 (Night 55, continuing directly from nights-54), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 55 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the stoker reach Damascus, where the stoker's wife dies; they join the caravan of the governor's tribute bound for King ʿUmar. Meanwhile his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān, who had left her brother in Jerusalem, is lured away by a Bedouin, beaten and carried off into the mountains. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْخَامِسَةُ وَالْخَمْسُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-khāmisatu wa-al-khamsūna
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the fifth and the fiftieth.
sentences.i: And when it was the fifty-fifth night,
sentences.n: The night formula; the compound ordinal ('the fifth and the fiftieth') stands in the nominative, as in the previous night.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْوَقَّادَ وَزَوْجَتَهُ اتَّفَقَا مَعَ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ عَلَى أَنَّهُمَا يَمْضِيَانِ مَعَهُ إِلَى دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-waqqāda wa-zawjatahu ittafaqā maʿa ḍawʾi al-makāni ʿalā annahumā yamḍiyāni maʿahu ilā dimashqa
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O happy king, that the stoker and his wife agreed with Ḍawʾ al-Makān upon that-the-two-of-them go with him to Damascus.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O happy king, that the stoker and his wife agreed with Ḍawʾ al-Makān that they would go with him to Damascus.
sentences.n: The edition prints السعيدان as one word, 'the happy' plus 'that' run together, and we keep it so; read it as al-saʿīdu anna. Shahrazād is the speaker, resuming the tale of the stoker (al-waqqād) who nursed the boy back to health.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَقَّادَ بَاعَ أَمْتِعَتَهُ وَأَمْتِعَةَ زَوْجَتِهِ وَاشْتَرَى جَمَلًا ثُمَّ اكْتَرَى حِمَارًا وَأَرْكَبَ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ إِيَّاهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-waqqāda bāʿa amtiʿatahu wa-amtiʿata zawjatihi wa-ishtarā jamalan thumma iktarā ḥimāran wa-arkaba ḍawʾa al-makāni iyyāhu
sentences.l: Then indeed the stoker sold his goods and the goods of his wife, and bought a camel, then hired a donkey, and made-ride Ḍawʾ al-Makān it.
sentences.i: Then the stoker sold his belongings and his wife's, bought a camel, hired a donkey, and set Ḍawʾ al-Makān upon it.
sentences.n: أَرْكَبَ is the causative (form IV) of 'ride', so it takes two objects: the boy, and the donkey (إِيَّاهُ, 'it').

sentences.t: وَسَافَرُوا وَمَازَالُوا مُسَافِرِينَ سِتَّةَ أَيَّامٍ إِلَى أَنْ دَخَلُوا دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: wa-sāfarū wa-mā zālū musāfirīna sittata ayyāmin ilā an dakhalū dimashqa
sentences.l: And they travelled, and they did not cease travelling six days, until they entered Damascus.
sentences.i: They set out and travelled on for six days, until they entered Damascus.
sentences.n: مَازَالُوا is printed joined here (two sentences on it is printed as two words, ما زالوا). It is the verb of continuance: 'they did not cease [being] travelling', that is, 'they went on travelling'.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلُوا هُنَاكَ فِي آخِرِ النَّهَارِ وَذَهَبَ الْوَقَّادُ وَاشْتَرَى شَيْأً مِنَ الْأَكْلِ وَالشُّرْبِ عَلَى الْعَادَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-nazalū hunāka fī ākhiri al-nahāri wa-dhahaba al-waqqādu wa-ishtarā shayʾan mina al-akli wa-al-shurbi ʿalā al-ʿādati
sentences.l: And they alighted there at the last-part of the day, and the stoker went and bought something of the eating and the drinking, according to the custom.
sentences.i: They put up there at the close of the day, and the stoker went out and bought some food and drink, as was his habit.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْحَالِ خَمْسَةَ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālū ʿalā dhālika al-ḥāli khamsata ayyāmin
sentences.l: And they did not cease upon that state five days.
sentences.i: And they went on in the same way for five days.

sentences.t: فَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ مَرِضَتْ زَوْجَةُ الْوَقَّادِ أَيَّامًا قَلَائِلَ وَانْتَقَلَتْ إِلَى رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-baʿda dhālika mariḍat zawjatu al-waqqādi ayyāman qalāʾila wa-intaqalat ilā raḥmati allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: And after that the wife of the stoker fell ill some few days, and passed over to the mercy of God the Exalted.
sentences.i: After that the stoker's wife fell ill for a few days, and then passed to the mercy of God Most High.
sentences.n: 'Passed over to the mercy of God' is the usual gentle way of saying that someone died.

sentences.t: فَعَظُمَ ذَلِكَ عَلَى ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ قَدِ اعْتَادَ عَلَيْهَا وَكَانَتْ تَخْدِمُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿaẓuma dhālika ʿalā ḍawʾi al-makāni li-annahu kāna qadi iʿtāda ʿalayhā wa-kānat takhdimuhu
sentences.l: And that was-great upon Ḍawʾ al-Makān, because he had become-accustomed upon her, and she used to serve him.
sentences.i: This weighed heavily on Ḍawʾ al-Makān, for he had grown used to her, and she had waited on him.
sentences.n: اعتاد عليها, 'grew accustomed to her', takes عَلَى (literally 'upon') here.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا مَاتَتْ حَزِنَ عَلَيْهَا الْوَقَّادُ حَزْنًا شَدِيدًا فَالْتَفَتَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ إِلَى الْوَقَّادِ فَوَجَدَهُ حَزِينًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā mātat ḥazina ʿalayhā al-waqqādu ḥuznan shadīdan fa-iltafata ḍawʾu al-makāni ilā al-waqqādi fa-wajadahu ḥazīnan
sentences.l: And when she died, the stoker grieved over her a severe grief, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān turned to the stoker and found-him grieving.
sentences.i: When she died, the stoker grieved over her bitterly, and Ḍawʾ al-Makān turned to him and found him sorrowful.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ لَاتَحْزَنْ فَإِنَّنَا كُلُّنَا دَاخِلُونَ مِنْ هَذَا الْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu lā taḥzan fa-innanā kullunā dākhilūna min hādhā al-bābi
sentences.l: And he said to him: Do-not-grieve, for indeed-we, all-of-us, are entering from this door.
sentences.i: He said to him: Do not grieve, for we shall all go in at this same door.
sentences.n: The edition prints لاتحزن ('do not grieve') as one word, and we keep it so. 'This door' is death.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ الْوَقَّادُ إِلَى ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَقَالَ لَهُ جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ خَيْرًا يَا وَلَدِى فَاللَّهُ تَعَالَى يُعَوِّضُ عَلَيْنَا بِفَضْلِهِ وَيُزِيلُ عَنَّا الْحُزْنَ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata al-waqqādu ilā ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-qāla lahu jazāka allāhu khayran yā waladī fa-allāhu taʿālā yuʿawwiḍu ʿalaynā bi-faḍlihi wa-yuzīlu ʿannā al-ḥuzna
sentences.l: And the stoker turned to Ḍawʾ al-Makān and said to him: May God requite you good, O my son; and God the Exalted will compensate upon us by His bounty and remove from us the grief.
sentences.i: The stoker turned to Ḍawʾ al-Makān and said to him: God reward you well, my son. God Most High will make it up to us out of His bounty, and take our grief away.
sentences.n: ولدى is printed with a final ى rather than ي; the word is waladī, 'my son'. 'May God requite you good' is a stock formula of thanks.

sentences.t: فَهَلْ لَكَ يَا وَلَدِي أَنْ تَخْرُجَ بِنَا وَنَتَفَرَّجَ فِي دِمَشْقَ لِيَنْشَرِحَ خَاطِرُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-hal laka yā waladī an takhruja bi-nā wa-natafarraja fī dimashqa li-yanshariḥa khāṭiruka
sentences.l: So is-there to you, O my son, that you go out with us and we take-a-stroll in Damascus, so that your heart may be eased?
sentences.i: Would you care, my son, to go out with me and take a stroll about Damascus, so that your heart may be lightened?
sentences.n: هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ …, literally 'is there to you that …', is an invitation: 'would you like to …?'. بِنَا, 'with us', here includes the speaker, so 'go out with me'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ الرَّأْيُ رَأْيُكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ḍawʾu al-makāni al-raʾyu raʾyuka
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: The opinion is your opinion.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: As you think best.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ الْوَقَّادُ وَوَضَعَ يَدَهُ فِي يَدِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَسَارَا إِلَى أَنْ أَتَيَا تَحْتَ اِصْطَبْلِ وَالِي دِمَشْقَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma al-waqqādu wa-waḍaʿa yadahu fī yadi ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-sārā ilā an atayā taḥta iṣṭabli wālī dimashqa
sentences.l: And the stoker rose and put his hand in the hand of Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and the two walked until the two came beneath the stable of the governor of Damascus.
sentences.i: The stoker got up, took Ḍawʾ al-Makān by the hand, and the two walked on until they came below the stables of the governor of Damascus.

sentences.t: فَوَجَدَا جِمَالًا مُحَمَّلِينَ صَنَادِيقَ وَفَرْشًا وَقُمَاشًا مِنَ الدِّيبَاجِ وَجَنَائِبَ مُسَرَّجَةً وَبَخَاتِيَ وَعَبِيدًا وَمَمَالِيكَ وَالنَّاسُ فِي هَرْجٍ وَمَرْجٍ
sentences.tr: fa-wajadā jimālan muḥammalīna ṣanādīqa wa-farshan wa-qumāshan mina al-dībāji wa-janāʾiba musarrajatan wa-bakhātiya wa-ʿabīdan wa-mamālīka wa-al-nāsu fī harjin wa-marjin
sentences.l: And the two found camels, loaded-ones with chests and furnishings and goods of brocade, and led-horses saddled, and Bactrian-camels, and slaves, and mamluks, and the people in tumult and confusion.
sentences.i: There they found camels laden with chests, with furnishings and brocade stuffs, saddled led-horses, Bactrian camels, slaves and mamluks, and the people all in bustle and confusion.
sentences.n: هَرْجٍ وَمَرْجٍ is a rhyming pair meaning 'turmoil and disorder'. جَنَائِب are horses led alongside, not ridden; بَخَاتِي are the heavy two-humped camels. The accusatives all depend on the verb 'found'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ يَاتُرَى لِمَنْ تَكُونُ هَؤُلَاءِ الْمَمَالِيكُ وَالْجِمَالُ وَالْأَقْمِشَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni yā-tarā li-man takūnu hāʾulāʾi al-mamālīku wa-al-jimālu wa-al-aqmishatu
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: O-one-sees, to whom are these mamluks and the camels and the cloths?
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: I wonder, whose are these mamluks, these camels and these stuffs?
sentences.n: يَاتُرَى is printed as one word; it is a stock phrase meaning 'I wonder'. تَكُونُ is feminine singular, though the things asked about are mamluks, camels and cloths together; Middle Arabic is loose about such agreement, and we vocalise what is printed.

sentences.t: وَسَأَلَ مِنْ بَعْضِ الْخُدَّامِ وَقَالَ لِمَنْ هَذِهِ التَّقْدِمَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-saʾala min baʿḍi al-khuddāmi wa-qāla li-man hādhihi al-taqdimatu
sentences.l: And he asked of some of the servants and said: To whom is this offering?
sentences.i: He asked one of the servants, saying: Whose is this present?

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْمَسْئُولُ هَذِهِ هَدِيَّةٌ مِنْ أَمِيرِ دِمَشْقَ يُرِيدُ إِرْسَالَهَا إِلَى الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ مَعَ خَرَاجِ الشَّامِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-masʾūlu hādhihi hadiyyatun min amīri dimashqa yurīdu irsālahā ilā al-maliki ʿumara ibni al-nuʿmāni maʿa kharāji al-shāmi
sentences.l: And the asked-one said to him: This is a gift from the emir of Damascus; he wants the sending of it to King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, along with the tribute of Syria.
sentences.i: The man he had asked said to him: This is a gift from the emir of Damascus, who wishes to send it to King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān together with the tribute of Syria.
sentences.n: al-masʾūl, 'the one asked', is the servant. al-Shām is Syria, here the province whose capital is Damascus.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ تَغَرْغَرَتْ عَيْنَاهُ بِالدُّمُوعِ وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ —
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa ḍawʾu al-makāni hādhā al-kalāma taghargharat ʿaynāhu bi-al-dumūʿi wa-anshada yaqūlu —
sentences.l: And when Ḍawʾ al-Makān heard this speech, his two eyes brimmed with the tears, and he recited, saying —
sentences.i: When Ḍawʾ al-Makān heard this, his eyes filled with tears, and he recited these verses —
sentences.n: تَغَرْغَرَتْ is said of eyes that fill and swim with tears; بِالدُّمُوعِ marks what they brim with. ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān is his own father, the king whose name he hears. The dash is the edition's, introducing the verse.

sentences.t:
اَيُّهَا الْغَائِبِينَ عَنْ جَفْنِ عَيْنِي * وَهُمْ فِى الْفُؤَادِ مِنِّي حُلُولُ
غَابَ عَنِّي جَمَالُكُمْ فَحَيَاتِي * لَيْسَ تَحْلُو وَلَا اشْتِيَاقِي يَحُولُ
اِنْ قَضَى اللّٰهُ بِاجْتِمَاعِي عَلَيْكُمْ * اَذْكُرُ الْوَجْدَ فِي حَدِيثٍ يَطُولُ
sentences.tr:
ayyuhā al-ghāʾibīna ʿan jafni ʿaynī * wa-hum fī al-fuʾādi minnī ḥulūlu
ghāba ʿannī jamālukum fa-ḥayātī * laysa taḥlū wa-lā ishtiyāqī yaḥūlu
in qaḍā allāhu bi-ijtimāʿī ʿalaykum * adhkuru al-wajda fī ḥadīthin yaṭūlu
sentences.l:
O you absent-ones from the eyelid of my eye * while they are in the heart of me, dwelling.
Your beauty has gone from me, so my life * is not sweet, and my longing does not change.
If God decrees my coming-together upon you * I shall recall the passion in a tale that is long.
sentences.i:
O you who are far from my eyes, yet dwell within my heart,
Your beauty is gone from me, and life has lost its sweetness, and my longing does not fade.
If God should grant that I be joined with you again, I shall tell my passion in a tale of great length.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse, and we copy the pointing exactly. In the first line الغائبين is printed in the genitive-accusative form after أَيُّهَا, where strict grammar would want the nominative الغائبون; the pointing is kept as the edition has it. فِى is printed with ى. 'Absent from the eyelid of my eye' means out of sight; the lovers are nevertheless 'dwelling' (ḥulūl) in the heart. لَيْسَ تَحْلُو, 'it is not sweet', uses laysa with an imperfect verb, which is slightly unusual.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ بَكَى فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi bakā fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu
sentences.l: And when he finished from his poetry he wept, and the stoker said to him:
sentences.i: When he had finished his verses he wept, and the stoker said to him:

sentences.t: يَا وَلَدِي نَحْنُ مَا صَدَّقْنَا أَنَّكَ جَاوَتْكَ الْعَافِيَةُ فَطِبْ نَفْسًا وَلَاتَبْكِ فَإِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكَ مِنَ النَّكْسَةِ
sentences.tr: yā waladī naḥnu mā ṣaddaqnā annaka jāwatka al-ʿāfiyatu fa-ṭib nafsan wa-lā tabki fa-innī akhāfu ʿalayka mina al-naksati
sentences.l: O my son, we not believed that-you came-to-you the well-being; so be-good in-soul, and do-not-weep, for truly-I I-fear for you from the relapse.
sentences.i: My son, we could hardly believe that health had come to you. Be of good heart and do not weep, for I fear a relapse for you.
sentences.n: جاوتك is printed so, with a waw, and the verb is not a form we can identify with confidence: it may be a slip for جاءتك ('came to you') or for جاوزتك ('passed over you'); either way the sense is that health has reached you. ما صدقنا means 'we scarcely believed'; طب نفسا, with the self in the accusative of specification, is the common idiom 'be of good cheer'. ولاتبك is printed as one word and is read wa-lā tabki, 'and do not weep'.

sentences.t: وَمَازَالَ يُلَاطِفُهُ وَيُمَازِحُهُ وَضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ يَتَنَهَّدُ وَيَتَحَسَّرُ عَلَى غُرْبَتِهِ وَعَلَى فِرَاقِهِ لِأُخْتِهِ وَمَمْلَكَتِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ الْعَبَرَاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-māzāla yulāṭifuhu wa-yumāziḥuhu wa-ḍawʾu al-makāni yatanahhadu wa-yataḥassaru ʿalā ghurbatihi wa-ʿalā firāqihi li-ukhtihi wa-mamlakatihi wa-yursilu al-ʿabarāti
sentences.l: And he did not cease being-gentle-with-him and joking-with-him, while Ḍawʾ al-Makān sighed and grieved over his exile and over his separation from-his-sister and his kingdom, and sent-forth the tears.
sentences.i: The stoker kept on soothing him and bantering with him, while Ḍawʾ al-Makān sighed and mourned his exile and his parting from his sister and his kingdom, and let the tears fall.
sentences.n: The subject of ما زال is the stoker; the 'while' clause that follows (ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ يَتَنَهَّدُ …) is a circumstantial clause, a new subject announced by و with its own verb.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتِ
sentences.tr: thumma anshada hādhihi al-abyāti
sentences.l: Then he recited these verses.
sentences.i: Then he recited these lines:

sentences.t:
تَزَوَّدْ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا فَاِنَّكَ رَاحِلُ * وَاعْلَمْ بِاَنَّ الْمَوْتَ لَا شَكَّ نَازِلُ
نَعِيمُكَ فِى الدُّنْيَا غُرُورٌ وَحَسْرَةٌ * وَعَيْشُكَ فِى الدُّنْيَا مُحَالٌ وَبَاطِلُ
اَلَا اِنَّمَا الدُّنْيَا كَمَنْزِلِ رَاكِبٍ * اَنَاخَ عِشِيًّا وَهُوَ فِى الصُّبْحِ رَاحِلُ
sentences.tr:
tazawwad mina al-dunyā fa-innaka rāḥilu * wa-iʿlam bi-anna al-mawta lā shakka nāzilu
naʿīmuka fī al-dunyā ghurūrun wa-ḥasratun * wa-ʿayshuka fī al-dunyā muḥālun wa-bāṭilu
alā innamā al-dunyā ka-manzili rākibin * anākha ʿishiyyan wa-huwa fī al-ṣubḥi rāḥilu
sentences.l:
Provision-yourself from the world, for truly-you (are) departing * and know that death, no doubt, (is) descending.
Your bliss in the world (is) delusion and regret * and your living in the world (is) impossible and vain.
Lo, the world (is) only like the halting-place of a rider * he knelt-his-camel in the evening, and he in the morning (is) departing.
sentences.i:
Take your provision from this world, for you are bound to depart, and know that death, beyond doubt, is coming down on you.
Your bliss in the world is delusion and regret, and your life in the world is a vain and empty thing.
The world is no more than a rider's camping-place: he kneels his camel at nightfall, and by morning he is gone.
sentences.n: The print points this poem, and we copy its marks exactly. Two spellings are the edition's own: فِى for فِي, and the verb in the last line, اَنَاخَ (anākha), 'he made his camel kneel', i.e. he halted for the night. مُحَالٌ means 'impossible, absurd'; said of a life, it means that the life itself is an illusion.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَعَلَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ يَبْكِى وَيَنْتَحِتُ عَلَى غُرْبَتِهِ وَالْوَقَّادُ يَبْكِى عَلَى فِرَاقِ زَوْجَتِهِ وَلَكِنَّهُ مَازَالَ يَتَلَطَّفُ بِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ إِلَى أَنْ أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ
sentences.tr: thumma jaʿala ḍawʾu al-makāni yabkī wa-yantaḥitu ʿalā ghurbatihi wa-al-waqqādu yabkī ʿalā firāqi zawjatihi wa-lākinnahu māzāla yatalaṭṭafu bi-ḍawʾi al-makāni ilā an aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu
sentences.l: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān began weeping and sobbing over his exile, and the stoker weeping over the separation from his wife; but he did not cease being-gentle with Ḍawʾ al-Makān until the morning became-morning.
sentences.i: Then Ḍawʾ al-Makān began to weep and sob over his exile, and the stoker wept for the loss of his wife; but he went on comforting Ḍawʾ al-Makān until morning came.
sentences.n: ينتحت is printed with a tāʾ; it is most likely a slip or a dialect form for ينتحب (yantaḥibu), 'sobs', and we read it so while keeping the printed letters. جعل + imperfect means 'began to'. Ending in ى, يبكى is the edition's spelling of يبكي; the same goes for فى elsewhere.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ قَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ كَأَنَّكَ تَذَكَّرْتَ بِلَادَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṭalaʿati al-shamsu qāla lahu al-waqqādu ka-annaka tadhakkarta bilādaka
sentences.l: And when the sun rose, the stoker said to him: As-though-you have remembered your lands.
sentences.i: When the sun had risen the stoker said to him: It seems you have been thinking of your homeland.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ نَعَمْ وَلَا أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُقِيمَ هُنَا وَأَسْتَوْدِعُكَ اللَّهَ فَإِنِّي مُسَافِرٌ مَعَ هَؤُلَا وَ الْقَوْمِ وَأَمْشِي مَعَهُمْ قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا إِلَى أَنْ أَصِلَ إِلَى بِلَادِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ḍawʾu al-makāni naʿam wa-lā astaṭīʿu an uqīma hunā wa-astawdiʿuka allāha fa-innī musāfirun maʿa hāʾulāʾ wa al-qawmi wa-amshī maʿahum qalīlan qalīlan ilā an aṣila ilā bilādī
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: Yes, and I-am-not-able that I stay here; and I-entrust-you to God, for truly-I (am) travelling with these and the people, and I-walk with them little, little, until I arrive at my land.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: Yes, and I cannot stay here. I commend you to God, for I am travelling with these people, and I shall walk along with them, little by little, until I reach my own country.
sentences.n: The edition prints هؤلا with a stray و after it (هؤلا و القوم); read it as هؤلاء القوم, 'these people', the hamza and the و having been displaced in the printing. أستودعك الله is the farewell formula 'I leave you in God's keeping'. قليلا قليلا, repeated, means 'little by little'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَقَّادُ وَأَنَا مَعَكَ فَإِنِّي لَا أَقْدِرُ أَنْ أُفَارِقَكَ وَأَنَا عَمِلْتُ مَعَكَ حَسَنَةً وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أُتَمِّمَهَا بِخِدْمَتِي لَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-waqqādu wa-anā maʿaka fa-innī lā aqdiru an ufāriqaka wa-anā ʿamiltu maʿaka ḥasanatan wa-urīdu an utammimahā bi-khidmatī laka
sentences.l: And the stoker said to him: And I (am) with you, for truly-I I-am-not-able that I part-from-you; and I have done with you a good-deed, and I-want that I complete-it by my service to-you.
sentences.i: The stoker said to him: Then I am going with you, for I cannot bear to part from you. I have done you one good turn, and I want to complete it by serving you.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ جَزَاكَ اللَّهُ عَنِّي خَيْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ḍawʾu al-makāni jazāka allāhu ʿannī khayran
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: May God requite you, on my behalf, (with) good.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said to him: May God reward you well on my behalf.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ بِسَفَرِ الْوَقَّادِ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa ḍawʾu al-makāni bi-safari al-waqqādi maʿahu
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān rejoiced at the travelling of the stoker with him.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān was glad that the stoker was to travel with him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَقَّادَ خَرَجَ مِنْ سَاعَتِهِ وَاشْتَرَى لَهُ حِمَارًا آخَرَ وَبَاعَ الْجَمَلَ وَعَبَّى زَادَهُ وَقَالَ لِضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ ارْكَبْ هَذَا الْحِمَارَ فِى السَّفَرِ فَإِذَا تَعِبْتَ مِنَ الرُّكُوبِ انْزِلْ وَامْشِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-waqqāda kharaja min sāʿatihi wa-ishtarā lahu ḥimāran ākhara wa-bāʿa al-jamala wa-ʿabbā zādahu wa-qāla li-ḍawʾi al-makāni irkab hādhā al-ḥimāra fī al-safari fa-idhā taʿibta mina al-rukūbi inzil wa-amshi
sentences.l: Then truly the stoker went-out from his hour, and bought for him another donkey, and sold the camel, and packed his provisions, and said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: Ride this donkey on the journey; and when you tire from the riding, get-down and walk.
sentences.i: Then the stoker went out at once and bought another donkey for him, sold the camel, and packed his provisions. He said to Ḍawʾ al-Makān: Ride this donkey on the journey, and when you grow tired of riding, get down and walk.
sentences.n: عبى is the Middle Arabic form of عبّأ, 'packed, made up (a load)'; the edition spells it with a final ى. من ساعته, 'from his hour', means 'at that very moment'. Note that ارْكَبْ and انْزِلْ and وَامْشِ are masculine singular imperatives, each speaking to Ḍawʾ al-Makān.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ بَارَكَ اللَّهُ فِيكَ وَأَعَانَنِي عَلَى مُكَافَأَتِكَ فَإِنَّكَ فَعَلْتَ مَعِي مِنَ الْخَيْرِ مَا لَا يَفْعَلُهُ أَحَدٌ مَعَ أَخِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ḍawʾu al-makāni bāraka allāhu fīka wa-aʿānanī ʿalā mukāfaʾatika fa-innaka faʿalta maʿī mina al-khayri mā lā yafʿaluhu aḥadun maʿa akhīhi
sentences.l: And Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: God has-blessed in you, and has-helped me to repay-you; for truly-you did with me of the good what no one does with his brother.
sentences.i: Ḍawʾ al-Makān said: God bless you, and help me to repay you; for you have done me a kindness such as no man does for his own brother.
sentences.n: بارك الله فيك and أعانني are perfects with the force of a wish ('may God bless you, and help me'); this optative perfect is regular and recurs.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَبَرَ إِلَى أَنْ جَنَّ الظَّلَامُ فَحَمَلَا زَادَهُمَا وَأَمْتِعَتَهُمَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْحِمَارِ وَسَافَرَا
sentences.tr: thumma ṣabara ilā an janna al-ẓalāmu fa-ḥamalā zādahumā wa-amtiʿatahumā ʿalā dhālika al-ḥimāri wa-sāfarā
sentences.l: Then he waited until the darkness grew-dark, and the two loaded their provisions and their goods on that donkey, and the two travelled.
sentences.i: Then he waited until darkness fell, and the two of them loaded their provisions and baggage onto the donkey and set out.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَالْوَقَّادِ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amri ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-al-waqqādi
sentences.l: This (is) what was of the affair of Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the stoker.
sentences.i: So much for the affair of Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the stoker.
sentences.n: A storyteller's formula for closing one strand before turning to the other; it is answered by وَأَمَّا … in the next sentence.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ أُخْتِهِ نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ فَإِنَّهَا لَمَّا فَارَقَتْ أَخَاهَا ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ خَرَجَتْ مِنَ الْخَانِ الَّذِي كَانَا فِيهِ فِي الْقُدْسِ بَعْدَ أَنْ الْتَفَّتْ بِالْعَبَاءَةِ وَخَرَجَتْ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ تَخْدُمَ أَحَدًا وَتَشْتَرِيَ لِأَخِيهَا مَا اشْتَهَاهُ مِنَ اللَّحْمِ الْمَشْوِيِّ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri ukhtihi nuzhati al-zamāni fa-innahā lammā fāraqat akhāhā ḍawʾa al-makāni kharajat mina al-khāni alladhī kānā fīhi fī al-quds baʿda an iltaffat bi-al-ʿabāʾati wa-kharajat li-ajli an takhduma aḥadan wa-tashtariya li-akhīhā mā ishtahāhu mina al-laḥmi al-mashwiyyi
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān: when she parted from her brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, she went-out from the inn which the two had been in, in Jerusalem, after she wrapped-herself in the cloak, and she went-out for the sake that she serve someone and buy for her brother what he had craved of the roasted meat.
sentences.i: As for his sister Nuzhat al-Zamān: when she had left her brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, she went out of the inn where the two of them had been staying in Jerusalem, having wrapped herself in a cloak, in order to take service with someone and buy for her brother the roast meat he had longed for.
sentences.n: The عباءة is the long outer cloak. Nuzhat al-Zamān means 'Delight of the Age'. The edition puts a shadda on التفّت, and we keep it: iltaffat, 'wrapped herself'. وأما … فإنها is the usual 'as for X … she …' construction, with فَـ introducing the main clause. القدس is Jerusalem.

sentences.t: فَخَرَجَتْ تَبْكِي وَهِيَ لَا تَعْلَمُ أَيْنَ تَتَوَجَّهُ وَكَانَ خَاطِرُهَا مَشْغُولًا عِنْدَ أَخِيهَا
sentences.tr: fa-kharajat tabkī wa-hiya lā taʿlamu ayna tatawajjahu wa-kāna khāṭiruhā mashghūlan ʿinda akhīhā
sentences.l: And she went-out weeping, and she not knowing where she should head, and her mind was occupied with her brother.
sentences.i: She went out weeping, not knowing which way to turn, her mind taken up with her brother.
sentences.n: خاطرها مشغولا عند اخيها: literally 'her mind (was) occupied at her brother', i.e. her thoughts were with him.

sentences.t: وَتَفَكَّرَتِ الْأَهْلَ وَالْأَوْطَانَ فَصَارَتْ تَتَضَرَّعُ إِلَى اللَّهِ تَعَالَى فِي دَفْعِ هَذِهِ الْبَلِيَّاتِ
sentences.tr: wa-tafakkarati al-ahla wa-al-awṭāna fa-ṣārat tataḍarraʿu ilā allāhi taʿālā fī dafʿi hādhihi al-baliyyāti
sentences.l: And she thought-of the family and the homelands, and she became supplicating to God the Exalted for the repelling of these afflictions.
sentences.i: She thought of her family and her homeland, and began to plead with God Most High to ward off these afflictions.
sentences.n: تفكرت is used here with a direct object, 'she called to mind'; Classical Arabic would more often say تذكرت. صار + imperfect, 'she came to be doing', is another way of saying 'she began to'.

sentences.t: وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: wa-anshadat taqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: And she recited, saying poetry.
sentences.i: And she recited these verses, saying:

sentences.t:
جَنَّ الظَّلَامُ وَهَاجَ الْوَجْدُ بِالسَّقَمِ * وَالشَّوْقُ حَرَّكَ مَا عِنْدِي مِنَ الْا آمِ
وَلَوْعَةُ الْبَيْنِ فِي الْاحْشَاءِ قَدْ سَكَنَتْ * وَالْوَجْدُ صَيَّرَنِي فِي حَالَةِ الْعَدَمِ
وَالْوَجْدُ اقْلَقَنِي وَالشَّوْقُ اَحْرَقَنِي * وَالدَّمْعُ بَاحَ بِمَا قَدْ كَانَ مُكْتَتِمِ
وَلَيْسَ لِي حِيلَةٌ فِي الْوَصْلِ اعْرِفُهَا * حَتَّى تُزَحْزِحَ مِنْ ضَعْفِي وَمِنْ سَقَمِي
فَنَارُ قَلْبِي بِالْاَشْوَاقِ مُوقَدَةٌ * وَمِنْ لَظَاهَا يَظَلُّ الصَّبُّ فِي نِقَمِ
يَا مَنْ يَلُومُ عَلَى مَا حَلَّ بِي وَكَفَى * اِنِّي صَبَرْتُ عَلَى مَا خُطَّ بِالْقَلَمِ
اَقْسَمْتُ بِالْحُبِّ مَا لِي سُلْوَةٌ اَبَدًا * يَمِينِ اَهْلِ الْهَوَى مَبْرُورَةُ الْقَسَمِ
يَا لَيْلُ بَلِّغْ رُوَاةَ الْحُبِّ عَنْ خَبَرِي * وَاشْهَدْ بِعِلْمِكَ اَنِّي فِيكَ لَمْ اَنَمِ
sentences.tr:
janna al-ẓalāmu wa-hāja al-wajdu bi-al-saqami * wa-al-shawqu ḥarraka mā ʿindī mina al-ā āmi
wa-lawʿatu al-bayni fī al-aḥshāʾi qad sakanat * wa-al-wajdu ṣayyaranī fī ḥālati al-ʿadami
wa-al-wajdu aqlaqanī wa-al-shawqu aḥraqanī * wa-al-damʿu bāḥa bi-mā qad kāna muktatimi
wa-laysa lī ḥīlatun fī al-waṣli aʿrifuhā * ḥattā tuzaḥziḥa min ḍaʿfī wa-min saqamī
fa-nāru qalbī bi-al-ashwāqi mūqadatun * wa-min laẓāhā yaẓallu al-ṣabbu fī niqami
yā man yalūmu ʿalā mā ḥalla bī wa-kafā * innī ṣabartu ʿalā mā khuṭṭa bi-al-qalami
aqsamtu bi-al-ḥubbi mā lī suluwatun abadan * yamīni ahli al-hawā mabrūratu al-qasami
yā laylu balligh ruwāta al-ḥubbi ʿan khabarī * wa-ishhad bi-ʿilmika annī fīka lam anami
sentences.l:
The darkness grew-dark and passion surged with sickness * and longing stirred what is with me of the pains.
And the anguish of parting in the entrails has settled * and passion has made me (be) in a state of non-existence.
And passion unsettled me and longing burned me * and the tear divulged what had been concealed.
And I have no stratagem in union that I know * until it removes something of my weakness and of my sickness.
For the fire of my heart with longings (is) kindled * and from its blaze the lover remains in torments.
O you who blame (me) for what has befallen me, and enough! * truly-I I-was-patient with what was written by the pen.
I swore by love, I have no consolation ever * the oath of the people of passion (is) fulfilled in its swearing.
O night, convey to the transmitters of love of my report * and bear witness by your knowledge that I, in you, have not slept.
sentences.i:
Darkness has fallen and passion is raging with my sickness, and longing has stirred up all the pains I have.
The anguish of parting has settled in my entrails, and passion has brought me to a state of nothingness.
Passion has unsettled me and longing has burned me, and my tears have given away what was hidden.
I know no stratagem for union, until something eases my weakness and my sickness.
The fire in my heart is kindled by longings, and in its flame the lover lives in torment.
You who blame me for what has befallen me, enough! I am patient under what the pen has written.
I swear by love that I shall never find consolation; the oath of lovers is a sworn oath kept.
O night, carry my tale to those who tell of love, and bear witness by your knowledge that I have not slept for you.
sentences.n: In line 1 the print divides the last word, الْا آمِ; it should be الآلام, 'the pains', and it seems to have lost a lām. In line 3, مُكْتَتِمِ is printed in the genitive (a rhyme-vowel) where grammar would want the accusative مُكْتَتِمًا. In line 4 the subject of تُزَحْزِحَ is not stated; we take it to be the stratagem, and the sense is rather obscure. In line 7, يَمِينِ is printed in the genitive for the rhyme, where grammar would want يَمِينُ. 'Written by the pen' is the common image of fate fixed in advance. All marks are the edition's own; we have copied them as they stand.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ نُزْهَةَ الزَّمَانِ أُخْتُ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ بَكَتْ وَصَارَتْ تَمْشِي وَتَلْتَفِتُ يَمِينًا وَيَسَارًا
sentences.tr: thumma inna Nuzhata al-zamāni ukhtu Ḍawʾi al-makāni bakat wa-ṣārat tamshī wa-taltafitu yamīnan wa-yasāran
sentences.l: Then indeed Nuzhat al-Zamān, sister of Ḍawʾ al-Makān, wept, and began walking and turning-about right and left.
sentences.i: Then Nuzhat al-Zamān, the sister of Ḍawʾ al-Makān, wept, and she went walking on, looking about her to right and left,
sentences.n: Nuzhat al-Zamān means 'Delight of the Age'; she has been left alone in Jerusalem while her brother lies sick. ṣārat + imperfect, 'she began to …', is a common way to start an action in this prose.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِشَيْخٍ مُسَافِرٍ مِنَ الْبَدْوِ وَمَعَهُ خَمْسَةُ نَفَرٍ مِنَ الْعَرَبِ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-shaykhin musāfirin mina al-badwi wa-maʿahu khamsatu nafarin mina al-ʿarabi
sentences.l: And behold, (there was) a sheikh, a traveller, of the Bedouin, and with him five persons of the Arabs.
sentences.i: when suddenly there appeared a travelling sheikh of the Bedouin, with five men of the Arabs in his company.
sentences.n: After wa-idhā, the bi- on شيخ only marks what appears: 'and behold, a sheikh'. نفر (nafar) is a counted group of men; خمسة نفر is 'five men'.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ ذَلِكَ الشَّيْخُ إِلَى نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ فَرَأَهَا جَمِيلَةً وَعَلَى رَأْسِهَا عَبَاءَةٌ مُقَطَّعَةٌ فَتَعَجَّبَ مِنْ حُسْنِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata dhālika al-shaykhu ilā Nuzhati al-zamāni fa-raʾāhā jamīlatan wa-ʿalā raʾsihā ʿabāʾatun muqaṭṭaʿatun fa-taʿajjaba min ḥusnihā
sentences.l: And that sheikh turned to Nuzhat al-Zamān and saw-her beautiful, and upon her head a cloak, torn-to-pieces, and he marvelled at her beauty.
sentences.i: The sheikh turned toward Nuzhat al-Zamān and saw that she was beautiful, though on her head was a tattered cloak, and he marvelled at her loveliness.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ إِنَّ هَذِهِ جَمِيلَةٌ تُدْهِشُ الْعَقْلَ وَلَكِنَّهَا ذَاتُ قَشَفٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla fī nafsihi inna hādhihi jamīlatun tudhishu al-ʿaqla wa-lākinnahā dhātu qashafin
sentences.l: And he said in his self: Indeed this-one (is) beautiful, bewildering the mind, but-she (is) possessor-of squalor.
sentences.i: He said to himself: This girl is beautiful enough to dazzle the mind, but she is in a wretched state.
sentences.n: في نفسه, 'in his self', is the usual way to say 'to himself'. قشف (qashaf) is squalor and hardship, the look of someone worn down by want.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كَانَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ أَوْ كَانَتْ غَرِيبَةً فَلَا بُدَّلِي مِنْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-in kānat min ahli hādhihi al-madīnati aw kānat gharībatan fa-lā budda lī minhā
sentences.l: So if she is of the people of this city, or is a stranger, there-is-no-escape-for-me from her.
sentences.i: Whether she belongs to this city or is a stranger here, I must have her.
sentences.n: The edition prints بدلي as one word; read it لا بدّ لي, 'I cannot do without', meaning 'I must have her'. We keep the glued spelling.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ تَبِعَهَا قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا حَتَّى تَعَرَّضَ لَهَا فِي الطَّرِيقِ فِي مَكَانٍ ضَيِّقٍ وَنَادَاهَا لِيَسْأَلَهَا عَنْ حَالِهَا
sentences.tr: thumma innahu tabiʿahā qalīlan qalīlan ḥattā taʿarraḍa lahā fī al-ṭarīqi fī makānin ḍayyiqin wa-nādāhā li-yasʾalahā ʿan ḥālihā
sentences.l: Then indeed he followed her little by little until he presented-himself to her in the road in a narrow place, and called her, in order that he ask her about her state.
sentences.i: Then he followed her little by little, until at a narrow place in the road he stepped into her path and called to her, to ask how she fared.
sentences.n: The li- in لِيَسْأَلَهَا is the purpose lām, 'in order to', and the verb after it is subjunctive. تعرّض لـ is 'to put oneself in someone's way'.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا بُنَيَّةُ هَلْ أَنْتِ حُرَّةٌ أَوْ مَمْلُوكَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahā yā bunayyatu hal anti ḥurratun aw mamlūkatun
sentences.l: And he said to her: O little-daughter, are you free or owned?
sentences.i: He said to her: My child, are you free, or a slave?
sentences.n: بُنَيَّة is the diminutive of بنت, 'daughter', a fatherly form of address to a young girl. The edition prints its vowel and shadda here, and we keep them.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُ نَظَرَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ بِحَيَاتِكَ لَا تُجَدِّدْ عَلَيَّ الْأَحْزَانَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmahu naẓarat ilayhi wa-qālat lahu bi-ḥayātika lā tujaddid ʿalayya al-aḥzāna
sentences.l: And when she heard his speech she looked at him and said to him: By your life, do not renew upon me the griefs.
sentences.i: When she heard his words she looked at him and said: By your life, do not make my sorrows fresh again.
sentences.n: بِحَيَاتِكَ, 'by your life', is an oath-like plea, 'I beg you'. The shadda on عليّ is the edition's own and is kept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا إِنِّي رُزِقْتُ سِتَّ بَنَاتٍ مَاتَ لِي مِنْهُنَّ خَمْسَةٌ وَبَقِيَتْ وَاحِدَةٌ وَهِيَ أَصْغَرُهُنَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā innī ruziqtu sitta banātin māta lī minhunna khamsatun wa-baqiyat wāḥidatun wa-hiya aṣgharuhunna
sentences.l: And he said to her: Truly-I, I was provided six daughters; there died to me of them five, and one remained, and she (is) the youngest-of-them.
sentences.i: He said to her: I was given six daughters, and five of them have died, and one is left, the youngest of them.
sentences.n: The sheikh's tale is a lie, told to win her trust; the narrator will say so plainly a few lines on. خمسة here is the numeral in its masculine-looking form, though the counted daughters are feminine.

sentences.t: وَأَتَيْتُ إِلَيْكَ لِأَسْأَلَكِ هَلْ أَنْتِ مِنْ أَهْلِ هَذِهِ الْمَدِينَةِ أَوْ غَرِيبَةٌ لِأَجْلِ أَنْ آخُذَكِ وَأَجْعَلَكِ عِنْدَهَا لِتُؤَا نِسِيهَا فَتَشْتَغِلَ بِكِ عَنِ الْأَحْزَانِ عَلَى إِخْوَانِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-atītu ilayka li-asʾalaki hal anti min ahli hādhihi al-madīnati aw gharībatun li-ajli an ākhudhaki wa-ajʿalaki ʿindahā li-tuʾā nisīhā fa-tashtaghila bi-ki ʿani al-aḥzāni ʿalā ikhwānihā
sentences.l: And I came to you to ask you: are you of the people of this city or a stranger? — for the sake that I take you and place you with her, that you keep-her-company, and she be-busied with you away from the griefs over her siblings.
sentences.i: I came to you to ask whether you belong to this city or are a stranger, because I want to take you home and put you with her, to keep her company, so that she may busy herself with you and forget her grief for her sisters.
sentences.n: The edition splits لتؤانسيها into لتؤا نسيها; we keep the split, and the word is li-tuʾānisīhā, 'that you keep her company'. اخوانها is literally 'her brothers' (or siblings), here her dead sisters. The verb in فتشتغل is the daughter's: 'that she be occupied with you', and the following بك uses bi- because اشتغل takes it for the thing one is busy with.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لَكِ أَحَدٌ جَعَلْتُكِ مِثْلَ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ وَتَصِيرِينَ مِثْلَ أَوْلَادِي
sentences.tr: fa-in lam yakun laki aḥadun jaʿaltuki mithla wāḥidatin minhunna wa-taṣīrīna mithla awlādī
sentences.l: So if there is not to you anyone, I will make you like one of them, and you become like my children.
sentences.i: And if you have no one in the world, I will treat you as one of my daughters, and you shall be as my own children.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ كَلَامَهُ قَالَتْ فِي سِرِّهَا عَسَى أَنْ أَمِنَ عَلَى نَفْسِي عِنْدَ هَذَا الشَّيْخِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat Nuzhatu al-zamāni kalāmahu qālat fī sirrihā ʿasā an amina ʿalā nafsī ʿinda hādhā al-shaykhi
sentences.l: And when Nuzhat al-Zamān heard his speech she said in her secret: Perhaps that I be safe for my self with this sheikh.
sentences.i: When Nuzhat al-Zamān heard his words she said to herself: Perhaps I shall be safe in this sheikh's care.
sentences.n: في سرّها, 'in her secret', is 'privately, to herself'. أمن على نفسه is 'to be safe as to oneself'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَطْرَقَتْ بِرَأْسِهَا مِنَ الْحَيَاءِ فَقَالَتْ يَاعَمِّ أَنَا بِنْتُ عَرَبٍ غَرِيبَةٌ وَلِي أَخٌ ضَعِيفٌ
sentences.tr: thumma aṭraqat bi-raʾsihā mina al-ḥayāʾi fa-qālat yā ʿammi anā bintu ʿarabin gharībatun wa-lī akhun ḍaʿīfun
sentences.l: Then she lowered with her head out of modesty, and said: O uncle, I (am) a daughter of Arabs, a stranger, and I have a brother, weak.
sentences.i: Then she bowed her head in modesty and said: Uncle, I am an Arab's daughter, a stranger here, and I have a sick brother.
sentences.n: أطرق برأسه is 'to lower the head'; the bi- joins the verb to the thing lowered. يا عمّ, 'O uncle', is how a young person politely addresses an older man. The edition prints ياعم as one word.

sentences.t: فَأَنَا أَمْضِي مَعَكَ إِلَى بِنْتِكَ بِشَرْطِ أَنْ أَكُونَ عِنْدَهَا بِالنَّهَارِ وَبِاللَّيْلِ أَمْضِي إِلَى أَخِي
sentences.tr: fa-anā amḍī maʿaka ilā bintika bi-sharṭi an akūna ʿindahā bi-al-nahāri wa-bi-al-layli amḍī ilā akhī
sentences.l: So I will go with you to your daughter, on condition that I be with her in the day, and in the night I go to my brother.
sentences.i: I will go with you to your daughter, on condition that I stay with her by day, and at night go to my brother.
sentences.n: Here بشرط أن is 'on condition that' (bi- gives the terms on which she goes); the two بـ in بالنهار وبالليل are the ordinary 'in the day, in the night'.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ قَبِلْتَ هَذَا الشَّرْطَ مَضَيْتُ مَعَكَ لِأَنِّي غَرِيبَةٌ وَكُنْتُ عَزِيزَةً فِي قَوْمِي فَأَصْبَحْتُ ذَلِيلَةً حَقِيرَةً
sentences.tr: fa-in qabilta hādhā al-sharṭa maḍaytu maʿaka li-annī gharībatun wa-kuntu ʿazīzatan fī qawmī fa-aṣbaḥtu dhalīlatan ḥaqīratan
sentences.l: So if you accept this condition I will go with you, because I (am) a stranger, and I was honoured among my people, and I have become abased, contemptible.
sentences.i: If you accept this condition I will go with you, for I am a stranger. I was honoured among my own people, and now I have become lowly and despised.
sentences.n: مضيت is a perfect in the conditional clause, standing for a future: 'I will go'.

sentences.t: وَجِئْتُ أَنَا وَأَخِي مِنْ بِلَادِ الْحِجَازِ وَأَخَافُ أَنَّ أَخِي لَايَعْرِفُ لِي مَكَانًا
sentences.tr: wa-jiʾtu anā wa-akhī min bilādi al-Ḥijāzi wa-akhāfu anna akhī lā yaʿrifu lī makānan
sentences.l: And I came, I and my brother, from the lands of the Hijaz, and I fear that my brother will not know for me a place.
sentences.i: My brother and I came from the lands of the Hijaz, and I fear he will not know where to find me.
sentences.n: The Hijaz is the region of Mecca and Medina. لايعرف is printed as one word, 'he will not know'; لي مكانا is literally 'a place for me', that is 'where I am'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْبَدَوِيُّ كَلَامَهَا قَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي فُزْتُ بِمَطْلُوبِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-badawiyyu kalāmahā qāla fī nafsihi wa-Allāhi innī fuztu bi-maṭlūbī
sentences.l: And when the Bedouin heard her speech he said in his self: By God, truly-I I have won with my sought-thing.
sentences.i: When the Bedouin heard her words he said to himself: By God, I have got what I wanted!
sentences.n: فاز بـ is 'to win, to obtain': the bi- marks the prize, so فُزْتُ بِمَطْلُوبِي is 'I have won my object'. The oath وَاللَّهِ opens his private speech.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَ إِلَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا مَابَقِيَ عِنْدِي أَعَزُّ مِنْكِ وَلَا أُرِيدُكِ إِلَّا لِتُؤَانِسِي بِنْتِي نَهَارًا وَتَمْضِي إِلَى أَخِيكِ مِنْ أَوَّلِ اللَّيْلِ وَإِنْ شِئْتِ فَانْقُلِيهِ إِلَى عِنْدِنَا
sentences.tr: thumma iltafata ilayhā wa-qāla lahā mā baqiya ʿindī aʿazzu minki wa-lā urīduki illā li-tuʾānisī bintī nahāran wa-tamḍī ilā akhīki min awwali al-layli wa-in shiʾti fa-inqulīhi ilā ʿindinā
sentences.l: Then he turned to her and said to her: There does not remain with me anyone dearer than you, and I do not want you except that you keep-company my daughter by day, and go to your brother from the first of the night; and if you wish, then carry him to at us.
sentences.i: Then he turned to her and said: No one is dearer to me now than you, and I want you only to keep my daughter company by day and go to your brother from the beginning of the night. Or, if you wish, bring him over to our place.
sentences.n: The edition prints مابقي as one word. إلى عندنا, 'to at us', is the Middle Arabic stacking of two prepositional words; read it 'to our place'. The li- in لتوانسي is the purpose lām, 'so that you keep company'.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلِ الْبَدَوِيُّ يُطَيِّبُ قَلْبَهَا وَيُلِينُ لَهَا الْكَلَامَ إِلَى أَنْ لَانَتْ لَهُ وَوَافَقَتْهُ عَلَى الْخِدْمَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazali al-badawiyyu yuṭayyibu qalbahā wa-yulīnu lahā al-kalāma ilā an lānat lahu wa-wāfaqathu ʿalā al-khidmati
sentences.l: And the Bedouin did not cease sweetening her heart and softening to her the speech, until she softened to him and agreed with him upon the service.
sentences.i: The Bedouin kept soothing her heart and speaking softly to her until she yielded to him and agreed to the service.
sentences.n: لم يزل + imperfect is 'he kept on …'. 'Sweetening the heart' (طيّب القلب) is Arabic for 'to comfort, to put at ease'.

sentences.t: وَمَشَى قُدْ امَهَا وَتَبِعَتْهُ فَغَمَزَ مَنْ مَعَهُ فَسَبَقُوهُ وَهَيَّأُوا الْهِجَانَ وَحَمَّلُوا عَلَيْهَا الْأَحْمَالَ وَوَضَعُوا فَوْقَهَا الْمَاءَ وَالزَّادَ
sentences.tr: wa-mashā qud āmahā wa-tabiʿathu fa-ghamaza man maʿahu fa-sabaqūhu wa-hayyaʾū al-hijāna wa-ḥammalū ʿalayhā al-aḥmāla wa-waḍaʿū fawqahā al-māʾa wa-al-zāda
sentences.l: And he walked in-front-of-her, and she followed him, and he winked-at those with him, and they went-ahead of him, and prepared the camels, and loaded upon them the loads, and put above them the water and the provisions.
sentences.i: He walked ahead of her and she followed; then he signalled to the men with him, and they went on before and made the thoroughbred camels ready, loading the packs on them and setting the water and provisions on top.
sentences.n: قد امها is printed as two words; it is قدّامها, 'in front of her'. الهجان (al-hijān) means white, high-bred camels. In the transliteration the split is shown as it is printed.

sentences.t: حَتَّى إِذَا وَصَلَ إِلَيْهِمْ سَيَّرُوا بِالْجِمَالِ وَسَافَرُوا
sentences.tr: ḥattā idhā waṣala ilayhim sayyarū bi-al-jimāli wa-sāfarū
sentences.l: Until, when he reached them, they set-going with the camels and travelled.
sentences.i: so that when he reached them they put the camels in motion and set out.
sentences.n: سيّر بـ is 'to set (the animals) going'; the bi- joins the verb to the camels it drives.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْبَدَوِيُّ ابْنَ زِنَاءٍ قَاطِعَ الطَّرِيقِ وَخَائِنَ الرَّفِيقِ وَحَرَامِيًّا صَاحِبَ مَكْرٍ وَحِيَلٍ لَا عِنْدَهُ بِنْتٌ وَلَا وَلَدٌ وَمَا كَانَ إِلَّاعَابِرَ طَرِيقٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-badawiyyu ibna zināʾin qāṭiʿa al-ṭarīqi wa-khāʾina al-rafīqi wa-ḥarāmiyyan ṣāḥiba makrin wa-ḥiyalin lā ʿindahu bintun wa-lā waladun wa-mā kāna illā ʿābira ṭarīqin
sentences.l: And the Bedouin was a son of fornication, a cutter-of-the-road, a betrayer-of-the-companion, and a robber, possessor-of cunning and wiles; not at him a daughter nor a child; and he was nothing but a passer-by-of-a-road.
sentences.i: The Bedouin was a bastard, a highwayman, a betrayer of his travelling-companions and a thief, full of cunning and tricks. He had neither daughter nor child, and was nothing but a man who waylaid travellers.
sentences.n: ابن زناء, 'son of fornication', is the standard word for 'bastard'. The sheikh's story of six daughters was a lie. قاطع الطريق is a highwayman; عابر طريق, 'a passer-by of the road', is a wayfarer, here one who preys on them. The edition prints إلا عابر as one word, الاعابر.

sentences.t: فَوَقَعَ بِهَذِهِ الْمِسْكِينَةِ لِأَمْرٍ قَدَّرَهُ اللَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-waqaʿa bi-hādhihi al-miskīnati li-amrin qaddarahu Allāhu
sentences.l: And he fell upon this poor-one, for a matter God had decreed.
sentences.i: and he fell in with this poor girl, by something God had decreed.
sentences.n: وقع بـ is 'to fall upon, to chance upon': the bi- marks what he came across. ل in لأمر is 'for, by reason of'. The shadda on قدّره is the edition's own.

sentences.t: وَلَا زَالَ الْبَدَوِيُّ يُحَدِّثُهَا فِى الطَّرِيقِ إِلَى أَنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ مَدِينَةِ الْقُدْسِ إِلَى ظَاهِرِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lā zāla al-badawiyyu yuḥaddithuhā fī al-ṭarīqi ilā an kharaja min madīnati al-Quds ilā ẓāhirihā
sentences.l: And the Bedouin did not cease talking to her in the road until he went out from the city of Jerusalem to its outside.
sentences.i: The Bedouin went on talking to her along the way until he had left the city of Jerusalem for the open country outside it.
sentences.n: ولا زال for the Classical ولم يزل (as in the sentence a few lines above) is a Middle Arabic variant: 'he did not cease'. القدس, 'the Holiness', is Jerusalem.

sentences.t: وَاجْتَمَعَ بِرُفْقَتِهِ فَوَجَدَهُمْ قَدْ جَهَّزُوا الْهِجَانَ فَرَكِبَ الْبَدَوِيُّ جَمَلًا وَأَرْدَفَهَا خَلْفَهُ وَسَارُوا اللَّيْلَ كُلَّهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ijtamaʿa bi-rufqatihi fa-wajadahum qad jahhazū al-hijāna fa-rakiba al-badawiyyu jamalan wa-ardafahā khalfahu wa-sārū al-layla kullahu
sentences.l: And he met with his company, and found them having prepared the camels, and the Bedouin mounted a camel and seated-her-behind, behind him, and they travelled the night, all of it.
sentences.i: He joined his companions and found them with the camels ready. The Bedouin mounted one camel and took her up behind him, and they travelled all night.
sentences.n: اجتمع بـ is 'to meet up with', with bi- naming the one met. أردفها is 'he seated her behind him on the same mount'; the خلفه that follows only repeats the sense.

sentences.t: فَعَرَفَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ أَنَّ كَلَامَهُ حِيلَةٌ عَلَيْهَا وَأَنَّ الْبَدَوِيَّ غَرَّهَا فَصَارَتْ تَبْكِي وَتَصْرُخُ طُولَ اللَّيْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿarafat Nuzhatu al-zamāni anna kalāmahu ḥīlatun ʿalayhā wa-anna al-badawiyya gharrahā fa-ṣārat tabkī wa-taṣrukhu ṭūla al-layli
sentences.l: And Nuzhat al-Zamān knew that his speech was a trick upon her, and that the Bedouin had deceived her, and she began weeping and crying-out the length of the night.
sentences.i: Nuzhat al-Zamān understood that his talk had been a trick played on her and that the Bedouin had deceived her, and she wept and cried out all night long.

sentences.t: وَهُمْ مُسَافِرُونَ فِى الطَّرِيقِ قَاصِدِينَ الْجِبَالَ خَوْفًا أَنْ يَرَاهُمْ أَحَدٌ
sentences.tr: wa-hum musāfirūna fī al-ṭarīqi qāṣidīna al-jibāla khawfan an yarāhum aḥadun
sentences.l: And they travelling in the road, making-for the mountains, in fear that anyone see them.
sentences.i: while they travelled on, making for the mountains, for fear that anyone should see them.
sentences.n: The edition spells fī here with a final ى (فى), as it often does; we keep it. قاصدين is a participle in the accusative describing how they travelled: 'heading for'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا صَارُوا قَرِيبَ الْفَجْرِ نَزَلُوا عَنِ الْهِجَانِ وَتَقَدَّمَ الْبَدَوِيُّ إِلَى نُزْهَةِ الزَّمَانِ وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا مَدَنِيَّةُ مَا هَذَا الْبُكَاءُ وَاللَّهِ إِنْ لَمْ تَسْكُتِي مِنَ الْبُكَاءِ ضَرَبْتُكِ إِلَى أَنْ تَهْلِكِي يَا كُورَةُ حَضَرِيَّةُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ṣārū qarība al-fajri nazalū ʿani al-hijāni wa-taqaddama al-badawiyyu ilā Nuzhati al-zamāni wa-qāla lahā yā madaniyyatu mā hādhā al-bukāʾu wa-Allāhi in lam taskutī mina al-bukāʾi ḍarabtuki ilā an tahlikī yā kūratu ḥaḍariyyatu
sentences.l: And when they became near the dawn they dismounted from the camels, and the Bedouin came forward to Nuzhat al-Zamān and said to her: O city-woman, what is this weeping? By God, if you do not fall-silent from the weeping, I will beat you until you perish, O kūra, townswoman!
sentences.i: When dawn was near they got down from the camels, and the Bedouin came up to Nuzhat al-Zamān and said: You city girl, what is all this crying? By God, if you do not stop your weeping I will beat you until you die, you town-bred wretch!
sentences.n: كورة is an insult whose exact sense is obscure here; it is plainly abusive, and it recurs. مدنية and حضرية both mean 'townswoman', a jibe at her softness in the eyes of a desert man. Nothing in the Arabic turns the beating threat into anything milder: ضربتك, a perfect, stands for 'I will beat you'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ نُزْهَةُ الزَّمَانِ كَلَامَهُ كَرِهَتِ الْحَيَاةَ وَتَمَنَّتِ الْمَوْتَ فَالْتَفَتَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا شَيْخَ النَّحْسِ يَا شَيْبَةَ جَهَنَّمَ كَيْفَ اسْتَأْمَنْتُكَ وَأَنْتَ غَدَرْتَنِي وَتُرِيدُ تُعَذِّبُنِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat Nuzhatu al-zamāni kalāmahu karihati al-ḥayāta wa-tamannati al-mawta fa-iltafatat ilayhi wa-qālat lahu yā shaykha al-naḥsi yā shaybata jahannama kayfa istaʾmantuka wa-anta ghadartanī wa-turīdu tuʿadhdhibunī
sentences.l: And when Nuzhat al-Zamān heard his speech she hated life and wished death, and turned to him and said to him: O sheikh of ill-fortune, O grey-hair of Hell, how did I trust you, when you have betrayed me and want to torture me?
sentences.i: When Nuzhat al-Zamān heard this she hated life and longed for death. She turned to him and said: You sheikh of ill luck, you grey head fit for Hell, how could I have trusted you, when you have betrayed me and now want to torture me?
sentences.n: استأمنتك is 'I took you to be trustworthy / put myself in your safe-keeping'. وتريد تعذبني runs two verbs together without 'an: 'you want you torture me', a Middle Arabic habit. شيخ النحس and شيبة جهنم are curses: 'sheikh of ill-omen', 'greybeard of Hell'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْبَدَوِيُّ كَلَامَهَا قَالَ لَهَا يَا كُورَةُ أَلَكِ لِسَانٌ تُجَا وِبِينَنِي بِهِ وَقَامَ إِلَيْهَا وَمَعَهُ سَوْطٌ فَضَرَبَهَا وَقَالَ إِنْ لَمْ تَسْكُتِي قَتَلْتُكِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-badawiyyu kalāmahā qāla lahā yā kūratu a-laki lisānun tujā wibīnanī bihi wa-qāma ilayhā wa-maʿahu sawṭun fa-ḍarabahā wa-qāla in lam taskutī qataltuki
sentences.l: And when the Bedouin heard her speech he said to her: O kūra, have-you a tongue, you answer-me-back with it? And he rose to her, and with him a whip, and struck her, and said: If you do not fall-silent, I will kill you.
sentences.i: When the Bedouin heard her he said: You wretch, have you a tongue to answer me back with? He got up and went at her with a whip and beat her, and said: If you do not keep quiet I will kill you.
sentences.n: The edition prints تجاوبينني as two words, تجا وبينني; read tujāwibīnanī, 'you answer me back'. الك is ألك, 'have you?' with the question-hamza unprinted. The relative clause has no linking word: 'a tongue you answer me back with'. بِهِ is the 'with' of instrument.

sentences.t: فَسَكَتَتْ سَاعَةً ثُمَّ تَفَكَّرَتْ أَخَاهَا وَمَا كَانَتْ فِيهِ مِنَ النِّعْمَةِ فَبَكَتْ سِرًّا
sentences.tr: fa-sakatat sāʿatan thumma tafakkarat akhāhā wa-mā kānat fīhi mina al-niʿmati fa-bakat sirran
sentences.l: And she fell-silent an hour, then she thought-of her brother and what she had been in, of the bounty, and wept in secret.
sentences.i: She fell silent for an hour, then thought of her brother and of the comfort they had once enjoyed, and wept secretly.
sentences.n: The shadda on سرّا is the edition's own. تفكّر is followed directly by its object, 'thought of her brother'. Here the 'hour' (ساعة) is a loose stretch of time.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ فِي ثَانِي يَوْمٍ الْتَفَتَتْ إِلَى الْبَدَوِيِّ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُ عَلَيَّ هَذِهِ الْحِيلَةَ حَتَّى أَتَيْتَ بِي إِلَى هَذِهِ الْجِبَالِ الْقَفِرَةِ وَمَا قَصْدُكَ مِنِّي
sentences.tr: thumma fī thānī yawmin iltafatat ilā al-badawiyyi wa-qālat lahu kayfa taʿmalu ʿalayya hādhihi al-ḥīlata ḥattā atayta bī ilā hādhihi al-jibāli al-qafirati wa-mā qaṣduka minnī
sentences.l: Then on the second day she turned to the Bedouin and said to him: How do you work upon me this trick, until you brought with me to these desolate mountains? And what (is) your aim from me?
sentences.i: Then on the second day she turned to the Bedouin and said: How could you play this trick on me, bringing me to these barren mountains? What do you want of me?
sentences.n: أتى بـ is 'to bring': the bi- marks the person brought, so أتيت بي is 'you brought me'. The shadda on عليّ is the edition's own.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ كَلَامَهَا قَسَا قَلْبُهُ وَقَالَ لَهَا يَا كُورَةَ النَّحْسِ أَلَكِ لِسَانٌ تُجَا وِبِينَنِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa kalāmahā qasā qalbuhu wa-qāla lahā yā kūrata al-naḥsi a-laki lisānun tujā wibīnanī bihi
sentences.l: And when he heard her speech his heart hardened, and he said to her: O kūra of ill-fortune, have-you a tongue, you answer-me-back with it?
sentences.i: When he heard her his heart hardened and he said: You wretch of ill luck, have you a tongue to answer me back with?

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَ السَّوْطَ وَنَزَلَ بِهِ عَلَى ظَهْرِهَا إِلَى أَنْ غُشِيَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: wa-akhadha al-sawṭa wa-nazala bihi ʿalā ẓahrihā ilā an ghushiya ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And he took the whip, and came-down with it upon her back, until it was covered over her.
sentences.i: He took up the whip and brought it down on her back until she fainted.
sentences.n: غُشِيَ عَلَيْهِ is the passive 'it was covered over him', the idiom for 'he swooned'. نزل بـ is 'to come down with (something) upon'.

sentences.t: فَانْكَبَّتْ عَلَى رِجْلَيْهِ وَقَبَّلَتْهُمَا فَكَفَّ عَنْهَا الضَّرْبَ وَصَارَ يَشْتُمُهَا وَيَقُولُ لَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-inkabbat ʿalā rijlayhi wa-qabbalathumā fa-kaffa ʿanhā al-ḍarba wa-ṣāra yashtumuhā wa-yaqūlu lahā
sentences.l: And she fell-prone upon his two feet and kissed them both, and he held back from her the beating, and began cursing her and saying to her:
sentences.i: She threw herself down at his feet and kissed them, and he held off beating her, but went on to curse her, saying:

sentences.t: وَحَقِّ طَرْطُورِي إِنْ رَأَيْتُكِ أَوْسَمِعْتُكِ تَبْكِينَ قَطَعْتُ لِسَانَكِ وَدَسَّتُهُ فِي كُسِّكِ يَا كُورَةُ حَضَرِيَّةُ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥaqqi ṭarṭūrī in raʾaytuki aw samiʿtuki tabkīna qaṭaʿtu lisānaki wa-dassatuhu fī kussiki yā kūratu ḥaḍariyyatu
sentences.l: By the right of my cap! If I see you or hear you weeping, I will cut your tongue and shove it in your cunt, O kūra, townswoman!
sentences.i: By my cap, if I see you or hear you crying again, I will cut out your tongue and shove it up your cunt, you town-bred wretch!
sentences.n: طرطور is the tall, pointed cap of Bedouin and rustic folk, and swearing by it is a coarse oath. The threat is as crude in Arabic as in English; كس is the common vulgar word. The perfect verbs قطعت ودسّته stand for the future in the threat. أو سمعتك is printed as one word, اوسمعتك; the edition's shadda on دسّته is kept.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ سَكَتَتْ وَلَمْ تَرُدَّ جَوَابًا وَآلَمَهَا الضَّرْبُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika sakatat wa-lam tarudda jawāban wa-ālamahā al-ḍarbu
sentences.l: And at that she fell-silent and did not return an answer, and the beating pained her.
sentences.i: At that she fell silent and gave no answer, for the beating pained her.

sentences.t: فَقَعَدَتْ عَلَى قَرَا فِيصِهَا وَجَعَلَتْ رَأْسَهَا فِي طَوْقِهَا وَنَظَرَتْ إِلَى حَالِهَا وَذُلِّهَا بَعْدَ عِزِّهَا وَمَا حَلَّ بِهَا مِنَ الضَّرْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qaʿadat ʿalā qarā fīṣihā wa-jaʿalat raʾsahā fī ṭawqihā wa-naẓarat ilā ḥālihā wa-dhullihā baʿda ʿizzihā wa-mā ḥalla bihā mina al-ḍarbi
sentences.l: And she sat upon her qarā-fīṣ, and put her head in her collar, and looked at her state and her abasement after her honour, and what had befallen her of the beating.
sentences.i: She sat huddled on her haunches with her head sunk into her collar, and looked at her plight, at her humiliation after her honour, and at what had befallen her through the beating.
sentences.n: قرا فيصها is printed as two words and is obscure. Perhaps it is a form of the root ق-ر-ف-ص, 'to squat', so 'on her haunches'; we vocalise it as printed and offer that only as a guess. طوق is a collar or neck-opening: she hunches her head into her garment. حلّ بـ is 'to befall'.

sentences.t: وَتَفَكَّرَتْ فِي حَالِ أَخِيهَا وَفِي مَرَضِهِ وَوَحْدَتِهِ وَاغْتِرَابِهِمَا
sentences.tr: wa-tafakkarat fī ḥāli akhīhā wa-fī maraḍihi wa-waḥdatihi wa-ightirābihimā
sentences.l: And she thought on the state of her brother, and on his sickness and his aloneness, and the exile-from-home of the two of them.
sentences.i: She thought of her brother's condition, of his illness and his loneliness, and of the exile of them both.

sentences.t: وَأَرْسَلَتْ دُمُوعَهَا عَلَى وَجَنَاتِهَا وَبَكَتْ سِرًّا وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ
sentences.tr: wa-arsalat dumūʿahā ʿalā wajanātihā wa-bakat sirran wa-anshadat taqūlu
sentences.l: And she sent forth her tears upon her cheeks, and wept in secret, and recited, saying:
sentences.i: She let her tears run down her cheeks, and wept in secret, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: أنشدت تقول, 'she recited, saying', introduces a poem. The verses themselves begin the next stretch of the night.

sentences.t:
مِنْ عَادَةِ الدَّهْرِ اِدْبَارٌ وَاِقْبَالُ * فَمَا يَدُومُ لَهُ بَيْنَ الْوَرَى حَالُ
وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ مِنَ الدُّنْيَالَهُ اَجَلُ * وَتَنْقَضِي لِجَمِيعِ النَّاسِ اَجَالُ
كَمْ اَحْمِلُ الضَّيْمَ وَالاَهْوَالَ يَا اَسَفِي * مِنْ عِيشَةٍ كُلُّهَا ضَيْمٌ وَاَهْوَالُ
لَا اَسْعَدَ اللهُ اَيَّامًا عُزِزْتُ بِهَا * دَهْرًا وَفِي طَيِّ ذَاكَ الْعِزِّ اِذْلَالُ
قَدْ خَابَ تَصَدِّي وَآمَالِي بِهَا انْصَرَمَتْ * وَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بِالتَّغْرِيبِ أَوْصَالُ
يَا مَنْ يَمُرُّ عَلَى دَارِيمَا سَكَنِي * بَلِّغْهُ عَنِّي اِنَّ الدَّمْعَ هَطَّالُ
sentences.tr:
min ʿādati al-dahri idbārun wa-iqbālu * fa-mā yadūmu lahu bayna al-warā ḥālu
wa-kullu shayʾin mina al-dunyālahu ajalu * wa-tanqaḍī li-jamīʿi al-nāsi ajālu
kam aḥmilu al-ḍayma wa-al-ahwāla yā asafī * min ʿīshatin kulluhā ḍaymun wa-ahwālu
lā asʿada Allāhu ayyāman ʿuziztu bihā * dahran wa-fī ṭayyi dhāka al-ʿizzi idhlālu
qad khāba taṣaddī wa-āmālī bihā inṣaramat * wa-qad taqaṭṭaʿa bi-al-taghrībi awṣālu
yā man yamurru ʿalā dārīmā sakanī * ballighhu ʿannī inna al-damʿa haṭṭālu
sentences.l:
From the habit of the age: a turning-away and a turning-toward; so no state endures for it among mankind.
And everything of the world has a term, and for all the people terms run out.
How long shall I bear the injury and the terrors — O my sorrow! — from a life all of it (is) injury and terrors.
May God not make happy days in which I was made-mighty for an age, while in the fold of that might was abasement.
My striving has failed, and my hopes through it have been cut off, and by banishment the limbs have been severed.
O you who pass by the house of what-was my dwelling, convey to him from me that the tears (are) pouring.
sentences.i:
It is the way of Time to turn away, then to turn back, and no state lasts for him among mankind.
Everything in this world has its appointed end, and the lifespans of all people run out.
How long must I bear wrong and terror, alas, in a life that is nothing but wrong and terror?
God grant no joy to those days in which I was exalted for a while, while within that glory lay humiliation.
My striving has come to nothing, my hopes are cut off, and exile has severed my limbs.
You who pass by the house where I once dwelt, tell him from me that my tears are streaming.
sentences.n: The poem rhymes throughout in -ālu (the final -u is the poet's pausal form; the first line's اِدْبَارٌ keeps its tanwīn and the others drop it for the rhyme). We copy the edition's pointing exactly. The edition prints الدُّنْيَالَهُ as one word, 'al-dunyā' plus 'lahu', and دَارِيمَا as one word, 'dār' plus 'mā'; both are kept. Read the last line as 'the house of my dwelling', or, if مَا is the relative, 'of him who dwelt in me'; the sense is that the speaker's tears are to be reported to the one who lived there. عُزِزْتُ is the passive 'I was made mighty'. تَصَدِّي is printed with fatḥa on the first letter and kasra under the second; it is a verbal noun of تَصَدَّى 'to apply oneself, to aim', here 'my striving'. The speaker is the captive woman, who recites this lament before the Bedouin.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا قَامَ إِلَيْهَا الْبَدَوِيُّ وَعَطَفَ عَلَيْهَا وَرَثَى لَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā qāma ilayhā al-badawiyyu wa-ʿaṭafa ʿalayhā wa-rathā lahā
sentences.l: And when she finished from her poetry, the Bedouin arose to her and inclined upon her and felt-pity for her.
sentences.i: When she had finished her poem, the Bedouin got up and went to her, showed her tenderness and pitied her.

sentences.t: وَمَسَحَ دُمُوعَهَا وَأَعْطَاهَا قُرْصَ شَعِيرٍ وَقَالَ لَهَا
sentences.tr: wa-masaḥa dumūʿahā wa-aʿṭāhā qurṣa shaʿīrin wa-qāla lahā
sentences.l: And he wiped her tears and gave-her a disc of barley and said to her:
sentences.i: He wiped away her tears, gave her a barley loaf, and said to her:

sentences.t: أَنَا لَا أُحِبُّ مَنْ يُجَاوِبُنِي فِي وَقْتِ الْغَيْظِ وَأَنْتِ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ لَاتُجَاوِبِينَنِي بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ هَذَا الْكَلَامِ الْفَاحِشِ
sentences.tr: anā lā uḥibbu man yujāwibunī fī waqti al-ghayẓi wa-anti baʿda dhālika lā tujāwibīnanī bi-shayʾin min hādhā al-kalāmi al-fāḥishi
sentences.l: I do not love one-who answers-me in the time of the rage; and you, after that, do not answer-me with anything of this speech, the obscene.
sentences.i: I cannot abide anyone who talks back to me when I am in a rage. From now on, do not answer me with any of this foul talk.
sentences.n: لَاتُجَاوِبِينَنِي is printed as one word: لَا 'not' joined to the feminine imperfect تُجَاوِبِينَ ('you answer') with the ـنِي 'me' attached; the doubled nūn is the final -īna of the verb plus the nūn that protects the verb before ـي. In Classical usage this would be a prohibition (لَا تُجَاوِبِي), but the indicative is kept as printed, and it works as 'you will not answer me'.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَبِيعُكِ لِرَجُلٍ طَيِّبٍ مِثْلِي يَفْعَلُ مَعَكِ الْخَيْرَ مِثْلَ مَا فَعَلْتُ مَعَكِ
sentences.tr: wa-anā abīʿuki li-rajulin ṭayyibin mithlī yafʿalu maʿaki al-khayra mithla mā faʿaltu maʿaki
sentences.l: And I — I-sell-you to a man, good, like me, who does with you the good, like what I did with you.
sentences.i: And I shall sell you to a good man like myself, who will treat you kindly, as I have treated you.
sentences.n: This is the Bedouin's threat: he will sell her on if she insults him again. The edition's wording is a grim joke, since his own 'kindness' is a barley loaf and the promise of a sale. In يَفْعَلُ the verb is indicative where Classical would give a relative clause with the same sense; the string is simply 'who does with you the good'.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ نِعْمَ مَا تَفْعَلُ
sentences.tr: qālat niʿma mā tafʿalu
sentences.l: She said: Excellent is what you do.
sentences.i: She said: Very well; do as you see fit.
sentences.n: The edition prints نعم, which could be read naʿam 'yes'; we read niʿma mā, 'excellent is what…', the standard way of approving an action. Either way she is simply giving in. The tone may be bitter.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا لَمَّا طَالَ عَلَيْهَا اللَّيْلُ وَأَحْرَقَتْهَا الْجُوعُ أَكَلَتْ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْقُرْصِ الشَّعِيرِ شَيْأً يَسِيرًا
sentences.tr: thumma innahā lammā ṭāla ʿalayhā al-laylu wa-aḥraqathā al-jūʿu akalat min dhālika al-qurṣi al-shaʿīri shayʾan yasīran
sentences.l: Then indeed-she, when the night grew-long upon her and the hunger burned-her, ate of that disc, the barley, a thing, small.
sentences.i: Then, as the night dragged on for her and hunger burned within her, she ate a little of that barley loaf.
sentences.n: وَأَحْرَقَتْهَا الْجُوعُ has a feminine verb with the masculine noun الْجُوع as subject; the edition's spelling is kept. Note that شيأ is printed with the hamza-carrying alif in this word.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا انْتَصَفَ اللَّيْلُ أَمَرَهُمُ الْبَدَوِيُّ أَنْ يُسَافِرُوا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā intaṣafa al-laylu amarahumu al-badawiyyu an yusāfirū
sentences.l: And when the night reached-its-middle, the Bedouin ordered them that they travel.
sentences.i: At midnight the Bedouin ordered his people to set out.
sentences.n: 'Them' is his party, who have not been named in this passage; the sense is that he gave the order to break camp and journey.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell-silent from the speech.
sentences.i: Then morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent.
sentences.n: The standard close of a night: the dawn catches Shahrazad mid-story, and she breaks off, leaving the tale for the next night.

sentences.t: الْمَبْ—احُ
sentences.tr: al-mab—āḥu
sentences.l: The mor—ning (?).
sentences.n: A stray printed fragment, with a dash standing where letters have dropped out. It looks like a damaged printing of الصباح 'the morning', or of a catchword, but we cannot recover it and do not guess; we keep the letters and dash exactly as printed.
